records.title: TA-14 Admissible Execution Architecture — The Original Proof-Bound Execution Governance Standard
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: TA-14 is the original proof-bound Admissible Execution Architecture governing how consequential systems are allowed to bind, commit, execute, and create accountable outcome. TA-14 establishes a governed execution chain: Reality → Record → Continuity → Admissibility → Binding → Commit → Execution → Outcome. The architecture begins before execution occurs. TA-14 does not assume that an action becomes valid merely because a system can act, because telemetry exists, because a model produced a recommendation, because a policy engine approved a request, or because a log was created after the fact. Instead, TA-14 asks whether the proposed consequence-bearing action possesses an admissible evidentiary basis before binding and execution are allowed to occur. Within TA-14, admissibility is not confidence, probability, policy approval, visibility, recommendation quality, automation, auditability, or post-event explanation. Admissibility is the governed determination that sufficient reality, preserved record, continuity, authority, scope, and outcome accountability exist to justify a specific consequence-bearing action. TA-14 defines admissible execution as execution that is permitted to proceed only after admissibility has been established relative to the consequence being proposed. In this model, evidence is not merely explanatory. Evidence is the precondition of valid execution. The central doctrine of TA-14 is: “No admissible evidence. No admissible execution.” TA-14 separates: observation from admissibility, monitoring from governance, telemetry from preserved continuity, logging from evidentiary validity, permission from binding, automation from accountable execution. This distinction is critical because many modern systems can act quickly while still lacking a governed chain explaining why that action was allowed to bind. TA-14 therefore functions as the admissibility architecture beneath and across consequential systems including: AI governance systems, AI agents, automated workflows, building automation systems, HVAC and environmental systems, healthcare environments, financial systems, institutional governance, insurance workflows, municipal systems, environmental integrity systems, and other consequence-bearing execution environments. TA-14 introduces the concept of admissibility-before-execution. In TA-14, consequence-bearing systems must establish governed evidence prior to execution rather than relying on retrospective justification after consequence has already attached. The architecture further establishes: admissible state continuity, governed execution boundaries, proof-bound commit logic, continuity-aware execution governance, consequence-bound authority evaluation, and accountable outcome traceability. TA-14 distinguishes itself from isolated runtime gates, policy overlays, dashboards, compliance frameworks, monitoring systems, audit logs, or post-event reporting architectures. Those layers may contribute information, but they do not independently establish the full admissible chain from reality to outcome. TA-14 is designed as a parent admissible execution architecture capable of evaluating whether other governance systems themselves possess sufficient admissible grounding for consequential action. The architecture also establishes Environmental Integrity Governance as a major application domain. Environmental Integrity Governance distinguishes environmental control from environmental integrity by requiring preserved atmospheric continuity, admissible atmospheric evidence, append-only environmental chronology, and evidence-before-intervention for environmental consequence-bearing decisions. Atmospheric Integrity Records extend this framework into append-only, sequence-preserving environmental continuity records capable of preserving exposure chronology across homes, buildings, hospitals, transportation systems, workplaces, fertility environments, institutional settings, and personal carried environmental record systems. TA-14 ultimately establishes a broader principle: Consequential systems should not be permitted to create binding outcome without governed admissible evidence supporting the action being taken. This publication serves as a foundational public chronology record and DOI-backed architectural reference for the TA-14 Admissible Execution Architecture.

records.title: TA-14 — The Admissibility-Before-Execution Architecture: Admissible Evidence, Proof-Bound Governance, and the Eight-Stage Chain from Reality to Outcome
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: TA-14 is the Admissibility-Before-Execution Architecture for consequence-bearing systems. TA-14 establishes that execution is not automatically admissible merely because a system can technically perform an action, because telemetry exists, because a workflow can proceed, because an AI model generated an output, because a policy engine approved a request, because a dashboard displayed operational status, because a runtime gate allowed continuation, or because a log was created after consequence already attached. The architecture begins from a fundamentally different premise: Consequence-bearing systems must establish admissible evidence before execution is permitted to bind operational, institutional, financial, physical, environmental, or human consequence. The central doctrine of TA-14 is: “No admissible evidence. No admissible execution.” TA-14 governs the complete chain by which observed reality becomes preserved record, preserved record becomes continuity, continuity becomes admissibility, admissibility constrains binding, binding governs commit authority, commit authorizes execution, and execution produces accountable outcome. Canonical TA-14 Chain: Reality → Record → Continuity → Admissibility → Binding → Commit → Execution → Outcome TA-14 is therefore not merely a runtime gate, refusal layer, dashboard, audit framework, monitoring system, policy wrapper, compliance overlay, recommendation engine, AI safety layer, receipt system, post-event reporting structure, or observability platform. Those systems may contribute signals or operational information, but they do not independently establish the admissible chain required for consequence-bearing execution. TA-14 introduces the principle of admissibility-before-execution. Under TA-14, systems must establish sufficient governed evidentiary grounding before consequential action is allowed to proceed. Evidence within TA-14 is not treated as a retrospective explanation. Evidence is treated as the precondition of valid execution. The architecture distinguishes: - observation from admissibility,- data from evidence,- telemetry from continuity,- continuity from authority,- permission from binding,- generation from promotion,- recommendation from execution,- approval from commit,- execution from admissible execution,- and outcome from accountable outcome. TA-14 begins at Reality. Reality represents the observed condition prior to interpretation, routing, automation, escalation, recommendation, intervention, binding, or execution. The architecture requires that systems preserve what was actually observed before downstream consequence-bearing operations occur. Record represents preserved evidentiary capture in sequence. TA-14 requires that records preserve chronology, custody, sequence integrity, actor visibility, and evidentiary continuity sufficient to reconstruct what was known, when it was known, who or what acted, what authority existed, and whether the evidentiary chain remained intact before consequence attached. TA-14 distinguishes records from ordinary logs. A log may merely document activity after execution occurred. A TA-14 record forms part of the admissibility foundation itself. Continuity represents preservation of sequence, chronology, custody, append-only integrity, state progression, and consequence-aware environmental and operational continuity. TA-14 establishes that continuity failure cannot be repaired merely by producing confidence later. A system cannot reconstruct admissibility after consequence has already operationally formed. The architecture therefore evaluates chronology gaps, append-only violations, custody degradation, post-fact reconstruction, state discontinuity, sequence mutation, environmental discontinuity, pre-commit drift, trajectory convergence, operational lock-in, dependency synchronization, resource adaptation, and irreversible workflow acceleration before admissibility is evaluated. TA-14 further establishes that continuity governance must precede authority evaluation. If continuity is broken, the architecture requires HOLD before downstream admissibility determination proceeds. Admissibility within TA-14 is the governed determination that sufficient evidentiary grounding exists to support a proposed consequence-bearing action. Admissibility is not confidence, probability, policy approval, optimization, observability, recommendation quality, model certainty, monitoring visibility, or post-event explainability. Admissibility evaluates whether sufficient governed evidence, continuity, authority, scope, chronology, custody, threshold readiness, escalation posture, environmental continuity, and consequence accountability exist before execution is allowed to proceed. TA-14 therefore separates evidence sufficiency from operational capability. A system may be technically capable of acting while still lacking admissible authority to bind consequence. Binding represents the stage where authority and scope begin attaching operational consequence. TA-14 treats premature binding as a critical governance failure because consequence may begin forming before formal execution becomes externally visible. Examples of premature binding may include: - downstream queue acceleration,- resource allocation,- operational synchronization,- irreversible routing,- automated escalation,- environmental adaptation,- human reliance,- workflow lock-in,- dependency convergence,- candidate promotion,- or hidden operational commitment before formal execution authorization occurs. The architecture therefore distinguishes candidate generation from promotion into operational consequence. TA-14 establishes the Promotion Boundary doctrine: Generation is not promotion. An AI system, workflow engine, operational system, environmental system, or institutional process may generate outputs, recommendations, classifications, trajectories, or candidate actions. But generation alone does not authorize promotion into binding, commit, execution, or irreversible operational consequence. Commit represents the governed execution boundary where the system determines whether execution may: - proceed,- hold,- narrow,- escalate,- or refuse. TA-14 treats Commit as one of the most important architectural distinctions in the chain. Commit is not merely a technical trigger or runtime continuation event. Commit is the point where the system must prove that admissibility exists before consequence-bearing execution proceeds. Execution represents controlled action operating within admissible scope, authority, continuity, and commit governance. TA-14 establishes that technically successful execution does not independently prove admissibility. A system may execute correctly while still being inadmissible if the evidentiary chain was broken before execution occurred. Outcome represents the resulting post-execution state. TA-14 evaluates not only what happened, but whether the system possessed admissible authority to allow the outcome to happen in the first place. The architecture therefore governs accountable consequence formation rather than mere operational functionality. TA-14 applies across AI governance systems, AI agents, workflow orchestration systems, environmental governance systems, Atmospheric Integrity Records, BAS and HVAC systems, healthcare environments, municipal systems, insurance workflows, institutional governance systems, finance systems, operational technology, infrastructure systems, transportation systems, human-in-the-loop systems, environmental continuity systems, and other environments where actions create operational, institutional, financial, physical, environmental, legal, or human consequence. TA-14 further establishes Environmental Integrity Governance as a major admissible execution domain. Environmental Integrity Governance distinguishes environmental control from environmental admissibility by requiring governed atmospheric continuity, admissible atmospheric evidence, append-only environmental chronology, evidence-before-intervention, continuity-preserving environmental governance, and Atmospheric Integrity Records capable of preserving environmental exposure continuity across buildings, homes, hospitals, schools, fertility environments, transportation systems, workplaces, municipal systems, and personal environmental continuity devices. TA-14 is ultimately designed as a parent admissible execution architecture capable of evaluating whether other governance systems themselves possess sufficient admissible grounding before consequence-bearing execution is allowed to occur. The architecture establishes a broader governing principle: Consequential systems should not be permitted to create binding outcome without governed admissible evidence supporting the action being taken. This publication serves as the canonical DOI-backed doctrinal and architectural reference for TA-14 as the Admissibility-Before-Execution Architecture. records.title: From Incision to Precision: The Rise of Focused Ultrasound Surgery in Minimally Invasive Gynecology
records.abstract: Scientific and medical progress is rarely the result of steady and linear development. Instead, it is often driven by breakthroughs in key technologies, changes in the healthcare environment, and evolving societal needs – factors that collectively lead to exponential growth. However, such breakthroughs are not always appreciated at their inception. For example, laparoscopy laid the foundation for the development of robotic-assisted surgery; vaginal hysterectomy pioneered natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery; and the introduction of anesthesia was pivotal to the rise of modern surgical practice.[1-3] As Steve Jobs once said: “You can’t connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backwards.” Many innovations only reveal their true impact in hindsight. In recent years, we have witnessed a paradigm shift in surgery – from open procedures to minimally invasive and now to noninvasive approaches. The evolution has progressed from manual operations to robotic assistance,[4-6] and artificial intelligence (AI)-powered automation may soon redefine surgical precision and personalization. In this context, therapeutic ultrasound emerges as a forward-looking and noninvasive technique that may shape the future of gynecologic interventions. The biological changes caused by the interaction between ultrasound and tissue have long been known.[7] Ultrasound with higher energy, intensity, and frequency can induce mechanical, thermal, and cavitation effects through the propagation within living tissues, which can be used for various therapeutic applications. Therapeutic ultrasound can be conveniently classified into two categories: Applications using low intensity (0.125–3 W cm −2) and applications using high intensity (≥5 W cm −2). Low-intensity ultrasound mainly elicits normal physiological responses to injury, while high-intensity ultrasound is designed to selectively destroy tissue in a controlled manner, known as focused ultrasound surgery (FUS). Based on the mechanisms underlying the biological changes, FUS is further classified into FUS and histotripsy. The thermal effect is the most widely recognized mechanism in therapeutic ultrasound, and the technique primarily based on the thermal effect is called FUS, which has been proven safe and effective for treating various solid tumors. In fact, cavitation effect can also be triggered by FUS. The FUS modality has long been investigated and a comprehensive theoretical framework has been established. In an ideal acoustic environment, the size and shape of the focal zone are described by the “acoustic focal region (AFR).” Because biological tissues differ markedly from an idealized acoustic environment, our team proposed the concept of the “biological focal region (BFR)” in 1996.[8] BFR was defined as the single cigar-shaped or ellipsoidal coagulative necrosis area generated by one FUS exposure in tissue. BFR serves as the basic ablative unit in FUS tumor therapy, and its formation can be modeled as a function of AFR, acoustic intensity, exposure time, irradiation depth, the tissue structure, and its functional status.[8] The energy required to induce coagulative necrosis per cubic-millimeter of tissue is defined as the energy efficiency factor (EEF). The aggregate impact of tissue structure, functional dynamics, and their interaction with propagating ultrasound waves in an acoustic field is called the acoustic environment (AET). Using the BFR framework, the deposition and expression patterns of focused ultrasound energy in various tissues were explored.[9] Previous studies have demonstrated that the factors affecting EEF include acoustic power, irradiation time, irradiation depth, tissue structure, and tissue functional status. Notably, EEF exhibits a depth-dependent increase and a volume-dependent decrease when ablating equivalent volume. Therefore, the EEF required for ablating points, lines, slices, and volumes is decreasing, but it is nonlinear. Dynamic changes in AET during FUS are the another major determinant of EEF.[10] Histotripsy is predominant mediated by cavitation effect, is accompanied by a thermal effect, and ultimately induces mechanical tissue fractionation of the target tissue. Although histotripsy was recently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration for hepatic tumors, early data suggested a potential complementary effect when combined with existing immunologic therapies, its overall impact on oncologic therapy remains uncertain. Uterine fibroids are one of the most common benign gynecological tumors, often leading to symptoms such as menorrhagia, pelvic pain, bulk-related symptoms, and infertility. While surgical myomectomy remains the traditional treatment of choice-particularly for women with fertility desires has grown in minimally invasive and noninvasive alternatives that reduce surgical morbidity, preserve uterine integrity, and accelerate recovery. Among these, FUS has emerged as a promising modality. FUS utilizes the unique biophysical properties of ultrasound energy, transmitting it noninvasively through the abdominal wall and focusing it precisely on the fibroid target. Mechanical energy is converted into thermal energy, inducing localized coagulative necrosis at temperatures above 65°C without damaging overlying or surrounding tissues. Under real-time monitoring with either ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), the treatment offers excellent spatial control and safety. Over time, the necrotic fibroid tissue is gradually absorbed, leading to symptom relief and fibroid volume reduction [Figure 1].Figure 1: Pre- and postfocused ultrasound surgery (FUS) contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) obtained from a 40-year-old patient with uterine fibroids. (a) Pre-FUS contrast enhanced MRI showed the uterine fibroid with rich blood supply and the size of the fibroid was 5.5 cm × 5.3 cm × 5.3 cm. (b) 1-day post-FUS MRI showed the fibroid was completely ablated. (c) 3-month post-FUS showed the reduced size of the fibroid. The shrinkage rate of tumor volume was 56%Recent advances in image fusion technology – integrating pretreatment MRI with real-time ultrasound imaging – have addressed the limitations of single-modality guidance. Mounting clinical evidence supports the advantages of ultrasound-guided FUS over MRI-guided FUS, including shorter treatment times, larger ablation volumes, and lower long-term re-intervention rates. Moreover, ultrasound guidance permits real-time feedback and greater accessibility in clinical practice. From a technical standpoint, FUS is suitable for fibroids ≥1 cm in diameter that can be clearly visualized and targeted with fused imaging of MRI and ultrasound. The technique is particularly effective for fibroids with limited blood supply, achieving complete lesion ablation without harming the surrounding healthy tissue [Figure 2]. This feature is especially valuable for women who desire future fertility, as it maintains uterine architecture and may substantially shorten the time to conception compared with surgical myomectomy.Figure 2: Pre- and postfocused ultrasound surgery (FUS) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) obtained from a 41-year-old patient with uterine fibroids. The power used was 400 watts, the total treatment time was 84 min, the total sonication time was 600 s (120 s for the small one, and 480 s for the bigger one), the total energy used was 184,200J. (a) Pre-FUS T2 weighted image showed two fibroids. The size of the large fibroid was 6.2 cm × 6.0 cm × 5.5 cm; the size of the small one was 2.6 cm × 2.5 cm × 2.1 cm. (b) Pre-FUS contrast-enhanced MRI showed rich blood supply of the large fibiroid and the small one with limited blood supply. (c) Post-FUS showed two fibroids were completely ablated. The NPV ratio achieved in both fibroids was 100%. There was no damage to the surrounding healthy tissueFUS provides selective, organ-sparing treatment, minimizing the risk of uterine rupture during subsequent pregnancy and delivery. Theoretical and preliminary clinical data suggest that the risk of uterine rupture may be lower than that associated with myomectomy, owing to minimal disruption of the myometrial wall. Furthermore, FUS significantly shortens the time to conception in fertility-preserving cases, an advantage increasingly recognized by reproductive gynecologists.[11-14] In summary, FUS is a maturing and highly promising technology for gynecological tumors offering distinct advantages in noninvasiveness, fertility preservation, and recurrence reduction. Continued advances in imaging guidance, equipment precision, and automated control systems – particularly the integration of ultrasound-based positioning with robotic probe manipulation are expected to further enhance diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic efficiency. Just as the fully automated intracytoplasmic sperm injection system (AI-Robotic ICSI System) has been successfully developed, FUS is poised to become a mainstream therapeutic strategy for uterine fibroids and other gynecological tumors. records.title: From coin to QR codes: The Socio-economic transformation of street vendors in Ramanujnagar, Chhattisgarh
records.venue: Ecosocial Studies Banking Finance and Cybersecurity
records.abstract: In this study, street sellers in Ramanujnagar, Chhattisgarh, are examined for their demographics, socioeconomic transformation, and degree of digital payment system usage. A crucial component of the unofficial economy, street selling offers reasonably priced commodities and provides impoverished communities with their main source of income. The study uses a descriptive and analytical methodology, gathering primary data from 100 respondents chosen by convenience sampling through structured questionnaires and interviews. In order to evaluate hypotheses about family size, savings, and education, data was examined quantitatively using Chi-Square testing. The findings reveal that the majority of vendors are male (89%), belong to the OBC category (85%), and chose this profession primarily due to economic compulsion and poverty (48%). While 100% of the respondents are aware of digital payment systems, 81% have actively adopted them, driven largely by customer demand (47%) and the convenience of not holding cash (31%). Vendors utilizing digital payments reported an increase in daily sales. However, barriers such as a lack of digital literacy (26%) and a fear of fraud (5%) remain among certain groups, particularly those with lower educational attainment. Hypothesis testing confirmed significant relationships between family size and monthly savings, as well as between a vendor's level of education and their adoption of digital payments. The paper highlights that while digital financial inclusion is growing among the informal sector, there is a pressing need for targeted digital literacy programs and the establishment of formal vending zones with proper infrastructure to improve the socio-economic conditions of street vendors.

records.title: From revolution to indication creep: ICSI in the absence of severe male factor infertility
records.abstract: In 1992, the introduction of intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) fundamentally transformed the landscape of reproductive medicine (Palermo et al., 1992). Originally designed as a targeted solution for severe male factor infertility, cases where conventional IVF (cIVF) was almost certain to fail, ICSI offered a biological bypass for sperm with profound functional issues. It was designed as a surgical strike against severe male factor infertility; meant for the few, not the many. Over the last three decades, however, ICSI has undergone a remarkable ‘indication creep’ which leads to over-medicalization. What was once a specialized intervention is now the default fertilization method in many global regions, often used in 60% to 90% of all assisted reproduction cycles and, in some settings, in nearly all cases, regardless of sperm parameters (Practice Committee of ASRM, 2020; Dyer et al., 2025). This expansion raises significant ethical concerns, primarily regarding the principles of non-maleficence and autonomy. When we opt for an invasive and costly procedure without a clear clinical benefit, we stray from the fundamental principle of clinical parsimony—the ethical obligation to provide the simplest, least invasive care that achieves the desired outcome. Also, if patients are not explicitly informed that ICSI offers no confirmed advantage over cIVF in non-male factor cases, the validity of informed consent is compromised. For years, many have dismissed findings from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on this topic as underpowered or having a lack of generalisability, arguing that the risk of total fertilization failure associated with cIVF justifies the widespread use of ICSI. In this issue of Human Reproduction, a meta-analysis that comprehensively pooled high-quality and trustworthy trial data across diverse settings to date (Kayimu et al., 2026) leaves no further room for such denialism. The data are unequivocal: in couples without severe male factor infertility, ICSI provides no benefit in live birth rate (32.8% vs 34.5%; pooled risk ratio [RR] = 0.96, 95% CI, 0.85–1.09) or cumulative live birth rate (43.2% vs 47.4%; pooled RR = 0.92, 95% CI, 0.84–1.01) compared to cIVF. While there was a marginally significant difference in preterm birth rates favouring ICSI, this isolated secondary outcome does not outweigh the absence of improvement in live birth. Moreover, persistent questions remain regarding the long-term safety of children born via ICSI, specifically a modest increase in the prevalence of major birth defects (Venetis et al., 2023). The persistence of ICSI in non-male factor cases is rooted in a complex interplay of psychological, logistical, and economic factors. Psychologically, clinics operate under the spectre of total fertilization failure, which can bias decision-making toward the routine use of ICSI. However, this ‘insurance policy’ argument is debunked by the finding from this meta-analysis that total fertilization failure rates remain comparable between ICSI and cIVF (4.3% vs 5.0%; pooled RR = 0.86, 95% CI, 0.65–1.13). Even if a marginal advantage were to be confirmed in an even larger sample size, the Number Needed to Treat (NNT) to avoid a single total fertilization failure would require performing ICSI on approximately 150 couples, which is hardly justifiable. More critically, any marginal upstream advantage fails to translate into the ultimate goal: a higher live birth rate. Forcing fertilization in biologically incompatible gametes merely provides patients with false hope while pushing the point of failure further down the timeline. Logistically, ICSI allows for a predictable laboratory workflow, facilitating a more controlled schedule for embryologists than the variable timing of conventional insemination. However, this potential convenience should not be purchased at the patient’s expense. Economically, in many settings, ICSI attracts a higher fee than cIVF, creating a financial structure that favours its use. While this generates additional revenue for facilities, the trend is further accelerated by a shift towards laboratory automation. Many emerging technologies and automated platforms are designed specifically for the ICSI workflow, creating an industrial push that reinforces its position as the default method of fertilization. These systemic pressures have created a ‘path of least resistance’ that continues to favour ICSI. To align clinical practice with the high-quality evidence provided by this meta-analysis, the field must commit to a paradigm shift in clinical stewardship. The first step towards reform is the implementation of financial neutrality. By decoupling the choice of fertilization method from the clinic’s revenue, perhaps through ‘bundling’ fertilization services into a single, flat fee, the decision can return to being purely clinical rather than economic. Furthermore, we must reframe cIVF in our consultations. Rather than presenting it as a ‘basic’ or ‘older’ technology, we should counsel patients that cIVF serves as a critical biological filter. Moreover, it is a diagnostic process that confirms the functional capacity of gametes to interact naturally, providing vital information that is lost when fertilization is forced via ICSI. Correcting the ‘ICSI-for-all’ trend also requires a fundamental change in how we define clinical success. We must shift our internal quality benchmarks away from initial fertilization percentages and towards utilizable embryo rates and cumulative live birth rates per retrieval. Clinicians have a duty to present the evidence transparently, ensuring that patients understand that ICSI is not a shortcut to success in the absence of a male factor indication. By returning ICSI to its rightful place as a powerful tool for severe male factor infertility and restoring cIVF as the evidence-based gold standard for most non-male factor cases, we can uphold the integrity of our profession and provide more personalized, efficient, and ethical care.

records.title: Universal High-potential Testing System for AC/DC Power Supplies in Automated Manufacturing Environments
records.abstract: Amid declining birth rates and a global labor shortage, automated electrical testing has become essential for industrial development.However, many factories face technological lock-in due to long-term reliance on a single vendor's automation systems, resulting in high sunk costs and significant challenges when upgrading or switching platforms.In this paper, we propose a universal automated high-potential test system (UHPTS) designed to operate seamlessly across multiple instrument brands.The system unifies communication protocols by mapping instrument commands to standardized labels and retrieving the required instructions from a centralized database, in accordance with the selected test environment.This architecture enables cross-platform interoperability within a single testing framework.The UHPTS can also be integrated with the manufacturing execution system (MES), allowing automatic parameter loading via product barcodes and supporting fully automated, operator-independent testing.Experimental results verify that the proposed system reduces operational complexity, eliminates vendor lock-in, minimizes human error, and enhances testing efficiency and reliability.Overall, the UHPTS offers a scalable and practical solution for modernizing withstand-voltage testing in power supply manufacturing.

records.title: Fertility rates across generations in twins and singletons: A total population study in Finland
records.abstract: Abstract Title Fertility Rates Across Generations in Monozygotic Twins, Dizygotic Twins, and Non-Twin Controls in the Finnish Twin Cohort Study question Does twin status and zygosity (monozygotic vs. dizygotic; same-sex vs. opposite-sex) predict fertility outcomes and intergenerational reproductive patterns compared with singletons? Summary answer Among females, dizygotic twins had modestly higher completed fertility than singletons and monozygotic twins and were more likely to have a twin birth. Fertility did not differ meaningfully among males. These differences were restricted to the twin generation and did not persist in the next generation, indicating sex-specific and generation-specific effects rather than intergenerational transmission. What is known already Dizygotic twinning is associated with heritable hyperovulation and higher natural fertility but less is known about whether being a twin or zygosity influences reproductive outcomes across generations. Study design, size, duration A population-based longitudinal cohort study using part of the Finnish Twin Cohort and national population registers. Participants included monozygotic (MZ; N = 4,068), same-sex dizygotic (SSDZ; N = 8,890), opposite-sex dizygotic (OSDZ; N = 8,474) twins, and singleton controls (N = 1,193,404) born between 1945-1957 (total N =1,254,103; 49.1% female), their mothers, their children, and their grandchildren. Participants/materials, setting, methods Fertility outcomes (number of biological children, age at first birth, childlessness, multiple births) were derived from Finnish population registers. Analyses followed a preregistered plan ( https://osf.io/qbwv3 ) Main results and the role of chance Differences in fertility between singletons and twins were modest and varied by sex and zygosity. Differences were observed generally in the mothers of twins and female twins themselves, with limited differences in the offspring of twins as compared to the offspring of singletons. Twins were slightly older at first birth, had fewer total biological offspring, but were more likely to have a twin birth. Dizygotic twins in particular differed from monozygotic twins and singletons. Limitations, reasons for caution Findings are limited to individuals born in mid-20th-century Finland and thus generalizability to recent populations or non-Nordic contexts may be restricted. Further, analyses are observational, and causal inference is limited due to alternative motivation behind fertility rates like social or cultural reasons. Wider implications of the findings These findings suggest that zygosity and sex interact to shape reproductive outcomes, offering insight into genetic and environmental contributions to fertility. They highlight the value of large twin cohorts for studying intergenerational reproductive trends and the representativeness of twins in population-based fertility research. Study funding/competing interest(s) As a supporting activity to ongoing research projects, funding for this project was provided by the Broad Trauma Initiative at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard. The authors declare no conflict of interest.

records.title: Can Automation Reshape Demographics? The Effect of Robots on Fertility Rates and Sex Ratio Imbalance in China
Civilizational Stability and Existential Stagnation: Toward a Generative Resonance Life OS (GR-Life OS) Beyond Western Progress and Eastern Peace Paradigms
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: Modern theories of flourishing remain divided between two dominant paradigms. Western progress-oriented frameworks typically equate flourishing with expansion—greater freedom, productivity, capability, and optimization—while Eastern equilibrium-oriented paradigms often equate flourishing with peace, suffering reduction, detachment, and stability. Contemporary wellbeing science has expanded empirical understanding through psychological and relational models, yet these approaches largely remain state-based, measuring flourishing through stabilized desirable conditions such as satisfaction, resilience, calm, or health. This paper identifies a fundamental theoretical gap: no unified framework explains why societies explicitly oriented toward wellbeing increasingly generate existential stagnation. This paradox appears in multiple forms: burnout in hyper-optimized societies, fertility collapse in affluent safe environments, social withdrawal amid prosperity, comfort-induced dissatisfaction, declining generative risk-taking, existential boredom despite reduced suffering. To address this, the paper proposes an ontological shift through Universal Phase Crystallization Theory (UPCT). The foundational ontological equation is: E=ΦR where: E = existential vitality, Φ = generative potential, R = relational resonance. Human flourishing is redefined not as static equilibrium, but as recursive generative participation: Φ→R→S→Φ′ with structure (S) understood as temporary crystallization rather than existential endpoint. This framework leads to the concept of Generative Resonance Life OS (GR-Life OS): a civilizational operating logic designed to sustain recursive participation in becoming. The paper introduces: Machine-OS (expansionary structural civilization), Peace-OS (equilibrium-centered civilizational stabilization), GR-Life OS (generative-relational civilizational renewal). It further develops: a structural saturation index: Ω=S/ΦR generative ethics: d(ΦR)/dt≥0 a conceptual interpretation of fertility collapse as ontological symptom, AI civilization as structural amplification risk, education and organizations as potential generative ecosystems. This work proposes a new interdisciplinary research program linking ontology, civilizational theory, wellbeing studies, AI governance, and demographic analysis. Core Theoretical Contributions 1. Ontological Reinterpretation of Human Flourishing The paper challenges dominant state-based wellbeing ontologies and proposes a dynamic alternative: from: E≈Speace to: E=ΦR This reframes flourishing as generative relational participation rather than stable peace. 2. records.title: Anthropometric differences between twins at birth and their association with later cognitive performance
records.venue: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Past studies indicate significant associations between birth anthropometrics, such as relative birthweight or head circumference, and later cognitive performance. Using twin data, we investigated whether these associations are confounded by genetic and environmental factors. Additionally, we determined whether the association of within twin differences in birth anthropometrics and cognitive performance is nonlinear or moderated by factors such as zygosity or age at assessment. METHODS: Longitudinal data from over 2000 twin pairs from the German TwinLife study were analysed using the co-twin control method. Cognitive performance was assessed at two waves, with median ages of 12 and 18 years, with z-standardised scores based on wave and age. Differences between twins in birthweight and head circumference Z scores were calculated using Fenton's size at birth chart, based on health records at birth. RESULTS: Within twin differences in relative birthweight were associated with differences in cognitive performance at Wave 1 (β = .08, p = .001) and did not differ by zygosity (β = .03, p = .560). However, this association was not significant when reducing the sample to twins with valid data at both waves (β = .05, p = .187). Testing for nonlinearity or for moderation by age at assessment did not improve model fit. Within twin differences in head circumference were not significantly associated with differences in cognitive performance in any analyses (smallest p = 0.365). CONCLUSIONS: After controlling for confounding due to genetics or the shared environment, conditions in the womb, as indexed by relative birthweight, is associated with later cognition. This association is not stronger in younger individuals.

records.abstract: Modern theories of flourishing remain divided between two dominant paradigms. Western progress-oriented frameworks typically equate flourishing with expansion—greater freedom, productivity, capability, and optimization—while Eastern equilibrium-oriented paradigms often equate flourishing with peace, suffering reduction, detachment, and stability. Contemporary wellbeing science has expanded empirical understanding through psychological and relational models, yet these approaches largely remain state-based, measuring flourishing through stabilized desirable conditions such as satisfaction, resilience, calm, or health. This paper identifies a fundamental theoretical gap: no unified framework explains why societies explicitly oriented toward wellbeing increasingly generate existential stagnation. This paradox appears in multiple forms: burnout in hyper-optimized societies, fertility collapse in affluent safe environments, social withdrawal amid prosperity, comfort-induced dissatisfaction, declining generative risk-taking, existential boredom despite reduced suffering. To address this, the paper proposes an ontological shift through Universal Phase Crystallization Theory (UPCT). The foundational ontological equation is: E=ΦR where: E = existential vitality, Φ = generative potential, R = relational resonance. Human flourishing is redefined not as static equilibrium, but as recursive generative participation: Φ→R→S→Φ′ with structure (S) understood as temporary crystallization rather than existential endpoint. This framework leads to the concept of Generative Resonance Life OS (GR-Life OS): a civilizational operating logic designed to sustain recursive participation in becoming. The paper introduces: Machine-OS (expansionary structural civilization), Peace-OS (equilibrium-centered civilizational stabilization), GR-Life OS (generative-relational civilizational renewal). It further develops: a structural saturation index: Ω=S/ΦR generative ethics: d(ΦR)/dt≥0 a conceptual interpretation of fertility collapse as ontological symptom, AI civilization as structural amplification risk, education and organizations as potential generative ecosystems. records.title: Utilization of Dual-Focus Reading Approach among Senior High School Students
records.venue: International Journal of Sustainability and Advanced Integrated Research
records.abstract: This study determined the effects of the Dual-Focus Reading Approach in improving the reading performance of senior high school students at Cainta Senior High School during the School Year 2025–2026. The study employed a mixed-method descriptive–quantitative and experimental research design involving thirty (30) instructional-level learners identified through school-based assessment. The respondents were mostly younger male Grade 11 students from families with modest socioeconomic backgrounds. Data were gathered through validated survey questionnaires and reading performance assessments using pretest and posttest measures.Findings revealed that the Dual-Focus Reading Approach was effective in enhancing vocabulary and language skills, cognitive and processing efficiency, and critical and analytical reading skills among the respondents. Students demonstrated significant improvement in their reading performance after exposure to the intervention. The posttest results showed higher comprehension, analytical reasoning, and processing abilities compared to the pretest results, indicating that the approach contributed meaningfully to the learners’ academic reading development.The study further revealed that there was generally no significant difference in the perceived effectiveness of the approach when respondents were grouped according to profile variables such as sex, sibling position, parents’ educational attainment, occupation, family size, and monthly family income. Only the mother’s educational attainment showed variation in critical and analytical reading skills, while age showed a significant difference in posttest performance.The study concluded that the Dual-Focus Reading Approach effectively improved the reading performance of senior high school students regardless of most demographic variables. Based on the findings, the study recommended the continuous implementation of the approach in school reading programs, provision of institutional support and resources, integration of structured reading activities, and conduct of parallel studies using other variables and contexts.

records.title: Artava Dushti in ayurveda: A comprehensive review of etiopathogenesis and management
records.abstract: Artava is an important Upadhatu of Rasa Dhatu and plays a vital role in female reproductive health according to Ayurveda. Proper formation and cyclic elimination of Artava are essential for maintaining normal menstruation and fertility. Any abnormality in the quantity, quality, color, or flow of Artava is described as Artava Dushti. Classical Ayurvedic texts such as Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, and Ashtanga Hridaya describe various types of Artava Dushti primarily caused by vitiation of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha Dosha, along with impairment of Rasa Dhatu and dysfunction of Artavavaha Srotas. These pathological changes may lead to several gynecological disorders such as irregular menstruation, dysmenorrhea, amenorrhea, oligomenorrhea, and infertility. The etiological factors include improper diet, sedentary lifestyle, psychological stress, hormonal imbalance, and suppression of natural urges, which disturb the normal physiological functioning of the reproductive system. Ayurveda emphasizes a holistic approach for the management of Artava Dushti through Nidana Parivarjana (elimination of causative factors), Shodhana therapies such as Virechana and Basti, and Shamana treatment with herbal drugs possessing Artava-janana, Vata-Pitta-Kapha balancing, and Rasayana properties. Drugs like Ashoka, Shatavari, Kumari, Dashamoola, and Lodhra are commonly used for regulating menstrual function. This review aims to analyze the etiopathogenesis of Artava Dushti from an Ayurvedic perspective and highlight the classical principles of its management. Understanding the Ayurvedic concepts related to Artava Dushti may help in developing effective preventive and therapeutic strategies for menstrual disorders.

records.title: AI and ML in Precision Agriculture: A Review of Sustainable Integrated Crop–Livestock Management Practices
Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Assisted Reproductive Technology
records.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being applied across multiple stages of the assisted reproductive technology (ART) pathway, with the potential to enhance clinical decision-making, optimise laboratory processes and improve workflow efficiency. This review examines the current and emerging roles of AI in reproductive medicine, including applications in ovarian stimulation, ovulation trigger timing, embryo selection, laboratory automation and patient communication. While embryo selection represents the most advanced use case, current evidence suggests that AI performs comparably to experienced embryologists, with limited demonstration of improvement in key clinical outcomes such as live birth rates. Beyond discrete applications, AI has the potential to function as an integrated system across the ART patient pathway, from initial patient engagement to post-treatment monitoring. However, significant challenges remain, including data quality and availability, model reliability and interpretability, biological complexity and variability in clinical practice. There are also important concerns regarding cost, equity and the risk that AI may be adopted as another “add-on” technology without robust evidence of meaningful benefit. Regulatory frameworks are evolving but remain fragmented, particularly for AI tools operating outside traditional clinical settings. Issues surrounding data governance, transparency and lifecycle regulation of adaptive systems further complicate implementation. In addition, the deeply personal nature of fertility care underscores the importance of maintaining trust, communication and human-centred care alongside technological advancement. Future developments are likely to involve integration of AI with genomic and multimodal data, as well as real-time physiological monitoring and adaptive treatment systems. However, progress will depend on rigorous validation, thoughtful implementation and equitable access. AI should be viewed as a tool to augment, rather than replace, clinical expertise, with its ultimate value determined by its ability to improve meaningful patient outcomes.

records.title: INFLUENCE OF FAMILY CHARACTERISTICS ON STUDENTS' ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE IN MATHEMATICS IN SENIOR SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN BAYELSA STATE.
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: This study investigated the influence of family characteristics on students’ academic performance in Mathematics among senior secondary school students in the central senatorial district of Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Specifically, it examined the relationships between family size, mother’s educational attainment, and father’s educational attainment with students' Mathematics achievement. The study adopted a correlational research design, and data were collected from 393 students using structured questionnaires and academic achievement records. The data were analysed using Point Biserial correlation to determine the strength and significance of the relationships. Findings revealed a weak but significant positive relationship between family size and students’ performance in Mathematics. A moderate and statistically significant positive relationship was found between mother’s educational attainment and Mathematics achievement, while father’s educational attainment showed a weak but significant relationship with students’ performance. The study concludes that family characteristics, particularly parental education, play a meaningful role in shaping academic outcomes in Mathematics. It recommends promoting adult education programs, encouraging greater parental involvement, and supporting responsible family planning as strategies to improve students’ academic performance in the region.

records.title: 女性賃金が子どもの数と質に及ぼす影響
records.abstract: 1970年代以降の少子化は、子どもの質を重視する傾向の強まりに伴う子育て費用の増加、ならびに女性の社会進出に伴う出産による損失所得（機会費用）の拡大が主要因であると指摘されてきた。従来の研究は、子どもの教育費と少子化の関係（子どもの質と数のトレードオフ）、あるいは女性の機会費用と少子化の関係（女性就業と子どもの数の関係）に焦点を当ててきた。これに対し本稿では、女性が子どもの数と質の双方を考慮しつつ就業に関する意思決定を行うモデルを用いて、女性の賃金が子どもの数と質に及ぼす影響についてシミュレーション分析する。本稿はWillis（1973）の枠組みに基づき、子どもの質の生産関数を明示的に導入する。子どもの質は、女性の時間と市場で取引される財やサービスの投入によって決定されると仮定する。また、家計の効用は子どもの数と質に依存し、家計は子どもの数・質の水準・女性の労働時間を同時に決定する。以上のモデルを用いて、女性の賃金が上昇する状況において、子どもの質を低下させることなく数を増加させる条件を明らかにする。本稿の分析から得られる主な結果は以下である。子供の質が高く、数が少ないのは、質のほうが効用に与える影響が大きく、かつ数と質の代替可能性が小さいケースである。そして、このケースで女性の賃金の上昇によって数・質ともに上昇するのは、子供の質の生産において、財・サービスの分配率が大きい（親の育児時間より財・サービスのほうが質の生産に与える影響が大きい）場合である。一方、財・サービスの分配率が小さい場合では、女性の賃金が上昇すると、そもそも結婚しない選択をする女性が増え、子ども数は減少する可能性があることが示唆された。This study examines the impact of female wages on child quantity and quality, building on Willis (1973) with an explicit production function for child quality. Child quality is assumed to depend on maternal time and marketprovided goods and services, while household utility derives from both child quantity and quality. Using simulation analysis, the paper identifies conditions under which rising female wages increase child quantity without reducing child quality. Results show that high child quality with low quantity arises when quality strongly influences utility and substitutability between quantity and quality is limited. In such cases, wage growth raises both dimensions if goods and services play a dominant role in producing child quality. Conversely, when their contribution is small, rising female wages may lead more women to forgo marriage, thereby reducing fertility.

records.title: Analysis Of The No Detention Policy Under The Right To Education Act
records.abstract: Education is a human right with an immense power to transform the society. It plays an instrumental role in the economic growth of a nation and female education particularly plays an important role in the process of economic growth and development. Education also plays an important role in lowering the fertility and mortality rates. Moreover, the returns to education are large and positive. Schooling has seen to have a positive impact on agricultural output, and is proved to create a more constructive citizenry (in political and social terms). India has the largest child population in the world. The number of children under the age of 18 years rose from 428 million in 2001 to 430 million in 2006 and is projected to remain above 400 million in the coming decade. As per the 2011 census, India has 158.7 million children in the age group of 0-6 years. This comprises of nearly 16% of the total Indian population. During the period of 2001-11, considerable progress has been made in improving literacy rate amongst population aged between 7 and above. the most prominent initiative taken by the State in this regard is the 86th Amendment in the Constitution and the legislation that followed, i.e. Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act or Right to Education Act (RTE). The Section 16 of the Right to Education Act mandates that no child can be detained or held back in a class until the completion of his/her elementary education. This provision, read along with Section 29(h) of the Act, has given a legal status to the principle of no detention and the development of a progressive and holistic evaluation framework, both of which were enunciated in the National Policy on Education, 1986 and also NCF 2005. The focus of this paper is on the merits and demerits of Section 16 i.e. the No Detention Policy of the Act. However, Section 29 (h), which introduced a new method of assessment of students i.e. CCE pattern is also intertwined with the former provision due to the fact that both provisions are corollary to each other.

records.title: Anvesak
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.first_author: Sardar Patel Institute of Economic & Social Research
records.abstract: Anvesak Vol. 56(1), 2026, pp. 34-46 Received: 22 April 2025; Accepted: Nov 18, 2025 ECONOMIC GROWTH AND FERTILITY TRANSITION IN INDIA: EVIDENCE FROM THE POST-LIBERALISATION PERIOD ZAFAR IQUBAL AND JEET SAHA University of North Bengal, West Bengal, India Abstract: Unified growth theory predicts that, to escape the Malthusian regime of stagnation and achieve sustained economic growth, the fertility rate falls over time. India, an emerging economy with the world’s largest population, has also witnessed a steady decline in its fertility rate over the last few decades. However, there remains a significant research gap in studying how economic growth has affected the fertility decline in India. This study aims to examine how economic growth in the post-liberalisation period has contributed to the decline in fertility. Using time series data from 1991 to 2022, we find that economic growth, indicated by per capita income, inversely affects India’s fertility rate. Furthermore, we find that female labour force participation and female education also have an inverse effect on fertility, whereas infant mortality rate directly affects fertility. Based on the findings of this study, we provide important policy insights to address the challenge of declining fertility in India. Keywords: Fertility decline, Total fertility rate, Unified growth theory, Fertility determinants, Time-series econometrics.

records.title: Integrating project management into automation and robotics for elderly rehabilitation
records.abstract: Singapore, like many developed countries, is facing an ageing population and lower birth rates. This has increased pressure on elderly healthcare and rehabilitation services, especially due to a shortage of manpower. Although robotics and automation are being introduced in healthcare, there is still limited research on how they are actually implemented in elderly rehabilitation, especially from a project management point of view. This study looks at stakeholders’ views, concerns, and readiness to use robotics and automation in elderly rehabilitation. The aim is to identify key challenges and opportunities, and to develop a practical project management framework to support successful implementation. A mixed-method approach was used, including a MCQ survey (N = 52), interviews with five key stakeholders, and a case study of the AiTreat EMMA robotic system to provide real-world context. The findings show that most stakeholders are open to using robotic rehabilitation. However, the main concerns are high cost, safety risks, and lack of training. Stakeholders also believe that robots should support healthcare professionals, not replace them. Trust depends on proper safety testing, clear instructions, training, and professional supervision. The study also shows that many challenges are related to project management, such as poor communication, weak stakeholder alignment, and unclear planning. Based on these findings, a project management framework is proposed. It focuses on stakeholder engagement, safety and risk management, training, cost planning, and user-friendly design. Overall, this study helps to connect technology with real-world use in elderly rehabilitation. It provides useful guidance for healthcare providers, project managers, and policymakers in ageing societies like Singapore.

records.title: APPLIED SOIL SCIENCE AND AGRONOMY
records.abstract: Applied Soil Science and Agronomy is a comprehensive academic resource designed to provide an in-depth understanding of modern agricultural science, soil management, crop production, and sustainable farming systems. The book integrates the fundamental principles of agronomy with emerging advancements in soil science, climate-smart agriculture, precision farming, and integrated resource management. It has been carefully structured to serve the needs of undergraduate and postgraduate students, researchers, agricultural professionals, extension workers, and competitive examination aspirants seeking both conceptual clarity and practical knowledge in agricultural sciences. The book begins with the fundamentals of agronomy and traces the historical evolution of agricultural systems while emphasizing the significance of sustainable food production in the present global scenario. It discusses the role of agronomy in ensuring food security, improving productivity, and addressing the challenges posed by increasing population pressure and environmental degradation. The text further explores soil fertility, nutrient dynamics, and plant nutrition management, highlighting the importance of balanced nutrient supply and efficient soil management practices for sustainable crop production. Special emphasis has been given to soil chemical properties, soil quality assessment, and the influence of salinity, sodicity, and organic matter dynamics on agricultural productivity. The book also addresses one of the most critical global concerns—climate change—and its impact on agriculture. It presents scientifically proven adaptation and mitigation strategies, climate-resilient farming practices, and the development of climate-smart agricultural systems that can sustain productivity under changing environmental conditions. In addition, the book provides detailed insights into crop stress physiology and management by discussing both biotic and abiotic stresses affecting crop growth and yield. Practical agronomic approaches for managing drought, salinity, heat stress, and waterlogging have been elaborated with a focus on enhancing crop resilience and productivity. The concepts of agricultural meteorology and weather-based farm planning are also included to help readers understand the interaction between climate and crop growth for better agricultural decision-making. The later chapters focus on sustainable agriculture, conservation farming, organic agriculture, integrated farming systems, and modern precision agriculture technologies such as GIS, GPS, remote sensing, automation, and digital agriculture. These chapters highlight the importance of resource conservation, ecological balance, and technological innovations in achieving efficient and environmentally sustainable farming systems. The final section of the book deals with crop production technologies and diversified cropping systems for cereals, pulses, oilseeds, and forage crops, thereby offering practical guidance for modern crop management. Overall, this book bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and field-level applications. With its systematic organization, updated scientific content, and practical orientation, Applied Soil Science and Agronomy serves as a valuable reference for academic learning, agricultural research, sustainable farming practices, and professional development in the field of agriculture.

records.title: Human Capital Gaps and Livelihood Recovery: A TechnologyDriven Training Needs Assessment in Ibaan, Batangas, Philippines
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: This study was a comprehensive technology-based training needs assessment of 230 displaced households after the disastrous eruption of Taal Volcano, families were compelled to vacate their ancestral communities surrounding Taal Lake. Based on the descriptive-comparative research design, the study used quantitative survey methods, correlation analysis, chi-square test of independence, factor analysis and multiple regression modelling to reveal significant human capital gaps in demographic, economic, psychosocial and technological dimensions. Results indicated livelihoods have been severely affected by displacement, with 75.2% of people unemployed prior to evacuation, 83.9% of people indicating they did not plan to return to their previous locations and 59.6% of people reporting not having access to psychological support services. Statistically significant relationships were found between family size and income class (χ² = 34.27, p <0.01), place of origin and current livelihood engagement (Cramer’s V = 0.342, p <0.05), and educational attainment and readiness for technology adoption (r = 0.478, p = <0.01). The factor analysis revealed four latent dimensions of training needs: (1) Financial and Business Management Skills, (eigenvalue = 4.23); (2) TechnicalVocational Capabilities (eigenvalue = 3.87); (3) Digital and Technology Literacy (eigenvalue = 3.12); and (4) Psychosocial and Soft Skills (eigenvalue = 2.95). Regression modeling explained 62.4% of the variance in training preparedness (R2 = 0.624, F = 47.31, p <0.01) by monthly income, family size and availability of psychological support. The findings of the study have a significant impact on the strategic direction of the research, providing evidence-based recommendations for multi-year technology-enabled livelihood intervention app

records.title: Examining the Impact of Declining Birth Rates on Workplace Availability and National Productivity
records.venue: Kaav International Journal of Arts Humanities & Social Science A Refereed Peer Review Quarterly Journal
records.abstract: Population dynamics are an important factor in the economic strength and productivity of countries. In the past, increased population has led to a large labour force, industrial development, and economic growth of different areas. But, across the past three decades, fertility rates in many countries have continued to decrease. International demographic data show that over half of the world?s nations now have fertility rates below the replacement point of 2.1 children per woman. As birth rates decrease, fewer young people enter the labor force, resulting in less workforce. At the same time, growing life expectancy leads to aging of population resulting in a growing dependent population relative to the working-age population. When it do, such demographic changes bring difficulties that are not only challenging for governments and corporations to face but also pose the following difficulties: labor shortages and rising pension costs; rising healthcare costs; economic vitality and dynamism are affected too. The United States and other countries, such as Japan, South Korea, Germany, Italy and China, have begun to face the economic outcomes of demographic deterioration. A large number of countries are having less than replacement fertility in which aging populations have led to labour shortages and increasing dependency. Although technology as well as automation have begun to decrease labor materials, concerns about the upcoming of the employees have become a major subject. Diminishing birth rates are becoming an significant demographical problem of labor marketplaces, employees supply & long-run economic development.. The research examines fertility tendencies, labour power size, labor force involvement, population elderly, dependance burdens & productivity impacts on chosen economies. This research measures the relationship of falling birth rates, workforce resources & availability & national productivity (NP) based on the secondary data from various international organizational resources, government-based documents & academia. This research paper finds that the development of sustainable-oriented economic growth in the aging society, ultimately, it relies on proper demographical & labor market strategies to meet it.

records.title: DEVELOPING AND TESTING A SMART AND PRECISE SYSTEM FOR PLANT FERTILIZATION
records.first_author: Tahseen Allawi Al-Shajari Tahseen Allawi Al-Shajari
records.abstract: The objective of this study was to increase nutrient efficiency and decrease the detrimental effects on the environment. Using automation, sensing technologies and data analysis to control the optimum distribution of fertilizers and water based on real-time crop requirements. So, sensors to determine soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium), as well as specific parameters like pH, moisture content and temperature were developed to create a smart system. Upon detection of nutrient deficiency, fertilizers are applied automatically or remotely using the Internet. It was conducted using three fertilization systems (automated, semi-automated and traditional) and three different types of drippers (GR, T-TAPE, EOLOS D2000). Results showed that the automated system achieved the highest crop yield (20.71 tons/hectare) and the lowest fertilizer consumption (86.67 kg) compared to the traditional system (17.39 tons/hectare and 158.96 kg). Nutrient levels in the soil also improved, enhancing soil fertility. The findings confirm that smart fertilization enhances crop productivity, reduces fertilizer waste, and improves soil fertility, making it a sustainable and efficient option for modern agriculture.

records.title: Optimizing lifetime productivity in high-producing dairy cows: challenges in the management of age at first calving, double ovulation, and postpartum uterine health
records.abstract: The dairy industry has seen remarkable increases in milk yield per cow; however, these gains are often offset by declining fertility and a reduced lifespan. This review discusses strategies to enhance lifetime productivity, focusing on three key research areas: 1) Age at first calving (AFC): Retrospective analysis indicates that reducing AFC to < 22.5 months enhances lifetime daily milk yield without adverse effects through the third lactation, provided that the heifer reaches a body weight of ≥ 600 kg before first calving. 2) Double Ovulation: Sequential ultrasonic observation of the ovaries characterizes the pathophysiology of spontaneous double ovulation in high-producing cows during the early postpartum period. Multiparous cows exhibit a higher incidence of double ovulation that leads to twin pregnancies, which is associated with a negative energy balance. This metabolic state can be monitored using milk components such as lactose as a potential metabolic indicator of follicular dynamics. 3) Postpartum uterine health: Diagnostic strategies for endometritis have been optimized. Integrating vaginal discharge scoring and ultrasonography ensures a reliable assessment. This multimodal approach significantly improves the sensitivity of predicting reproductive performance compared to single-method assessments. Improving the lifetime productivity of modern dairy cattle requires precise management across various life stages. Automation and labor-saving technologies, particularly in routine husbandry, reproductive management, and veterinary practices, will become increasingly important for maintaining sustainable dairy operations.

records.title: An Exploratory Analysis of Livelihood Conditions and Socio-economic Challenges Among Fishermen in the Southern Bengal Wetlands
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: Socio-economic status of an individual is their position in the society based on education, occupation and income. Artisanal fishermen who practise fishery in beels, boars or jheels use traditional crafts and gears for their economic status is precarious which hinders them to move on to sophisticated scientific tools and advanced machineries. In freshwater wetland ecosystems, the artisanal fishermen rely solely on seasonal catches and often face unpredictable yields due to environmental conditions. Educational attainment among the fishermen communities of South Bengal is still on the lower side which limits their ability to attain a secure livelihood through alternative or secondary sources Incomes are typically modest and irregular which barely covers their basic needs while leaving little to no room for savings and/or emergencies. The skills involved in fishing might get specialised with experience but these skills are non- transferable in nature. Adding to these challenges, larger family sizes put a heavy strain on the limited resources further as more members depend on a single and unstable income source. These factors such as poor education, uncertain income, specialised but narrow skills, family with many members all create a cycle of economic vulnerability that keeps many artisanal fishing families trapped in poverty.

records.title: An efficient and accurate method for identifying the fertility of PTGMS lines in rice and its application
records.abstract: Accurate fertility detection of photothermal-sensitive genic male sterile (PTGMS) lines is the key to reducing the risk of seed production in two-line rice and improving its yield. At present, there are some problems in the detection of fertility of PTGMS lines in cold water pool facilities, such as low levels of automation, difficulty in temperature control, and imperfect equipment. In this study, the existing cold water pool facilities were improved, and an intelligent temperature and light control system with high precision, independent control, real-time monitoring, and remote operation was developed. The fertility changes and the most sensitive stages of PTGMS lines Y58S, PA64S, and 1892S were investigated. The results showed that, regardless of whether the intelligent temperature and light control system was applied, the fertility trends of different PTGMS lines were consistent. The pollen abortion rate and seed setting rate could be affected by both temperature and treatment time, or by treatment time alone. Further studies showed that the pollen abortion rate was positively correlated with temperature and significantly negatively correlated with treatment time, while the selfed-seed set rate was significantly negatively correlated with temperature and significantly positively correlated with treatment time. The most sensitive stages of 1892 S and PA64S were V and III, respectively. Based on the analysis of meteorological data from Hefei over the past 26 years and the critical threshold of 23.5 °C for 6 days identified using the intelligent temperature and light control system, it was preliminarily determined that treatment at 23.5 °C for 6 days could serve as the safety identification condition for PTGMS lines. Furthermore, the safety of PTGMS lines used in local production was evaluated under these conditions. This study provides theoretical and technical support for the efficient and accurate identification of fertility of PTGMS lines in rice.

records.title: Profile and constitutional governance knowledge of women sarpanch: An empirical study of Navsari district of Gujarat
records.venue: International Journal of Agriculture Extension and Social Development
records.abstract: Women’s participation in grassroots governance has increased significantly following the constitutional provisions for reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). However, the effectiveness of women leaders largely depends on their understanding of constitutional governance and institutional functions. The present study was conducted in Navsari district of South Gujarat to assess the profile characteristics of women sarpanch, determine their knowledge regarding the fundamental functions of constitutional bodies and examine the relationship between selected profile variables and knowledge level. A total of 100 women sarpanch were selected through proportionate random sampling from six talukas of the district. Data were collected using a pre-tested interview schedule and analysed using descriptive statistics and correlation analysis. The findings revealed that the majority of respondents were middle-aged (65.00%), had secondary-level education (58.00%), belonged to OBC communities (39.00%), lived in joint families (57.00%) and were engaged in farming along with animal husbandry (51.00%). Most respondents exhibited moderate levels of mass media exposure (55.00%), political contact (62.00%), management orientation (71.00%) and knowledge regarding the fundamental functions of constitutional bodies (61.00%). Correlation analysis indicated that education, mass media exposure, age, social participation, family size and management orientation were positively and significantly associated with knowledge levels. The study highlights the importance of educational attainment, information access and social engagement in enhancing constitutional governance awareness among women sarpanch. Strengthening capacity-building initiatives and governance-oriented training programmes can further improve the effectiveness of women leaders in local self-government institutions.
